questions.text: If f(x) = |x| + |x − 1|, then which of the following is correct?
options: f(x) is both continuous and differentiable at x = 0 and x = 1.
f(x) is differentiable but not continuous at x = 0 and x = 1.
f(x) is continuous but not differentiable at x = 0 and x = 1.
f(x) is neither continuous nor differentiable at x = 0 and x = 1.
questions.solution: A sum of modulus functions is continuous everywhere. The graph has corners at x = 0 and x = 1 (left and right derivatives differ: −2 and 0 at x = 0; 0 and 2 at x = 1).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Let Z be the set of integers. A function f : Z → Z defined as f(x) = 3x − 5, ∀ x ∈ Z, is a bijective.
Reason (R): A function is a bijective if it is both surjective and injective.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: f is one-one, but not onto: 3x − 5 = 0 has no integer solution. So A is false; R is the definition of a bijection, so it is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): f(x) = 3x − 8 for x ≤ 5 and 2k for x > 5 is continuous at x = 5 for k = 5/2.
Reason (R): For a function f to be continuous at x = a, lim(x→a⁻) f(x) = lim(x→a⁺) f(x) = f(a).
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Continuity at 5 needs 2k = 3(5) − 8 = 7, so k = 7/2, not 5/2. A is false; R is true.

questions.text: The diagonals of a parallelogram are given by a = 2i − j + k and b = i + 3j − k. Find the area of the parallelogram.
questions.solution: Area = ½ |a × b|. The i-component is (−1)(−1) − (1)(3) = −2, the j-component is −[(2)(−1) − (1)(1)] = 3 and the k-component is (2)(3) − (−1)(1) = 7, so a × b = −2i + 3j + 7k with |a × b| = √62. Area = √62/2 square units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Solve the following linear programming problem graphically :
Maximise Z = x + 2y
subject to the constraints : x − y ≥ 0, x − 2y ≥ −2, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.
questions.solution: The lines y = x and x − 2y = −2 meet at (2, 2). The feasible region lies below both lines in the first quadrant and is unbounded, with corner points (0, 0) and (2, 2), where Z = 0 and Z = 6. The half-plane x + 2y > 6 has points in the feasible region (for example (10, 0) gives Z = 10), and Z grows without limit along y = (x + 2)/2. So Z has no maximum value.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find : ∫ (x + sin x)/(1 + cos x) dx
questions.solution: 1 + cos x = 2cos²(x/2) and sin x = 2 sin(x/2)cos(x/2), so the integrand is (x/2)sec²(x/2) + tan(x/2). By parts, ∫(x/2)sec²(x/2) dx = x tan(x/2) − ∫ tan(x/2) dx. Adding, the integral is x tan(x/2) + C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Evaluate : ∫ from 0 to π/4 of dx / (cos³x √(2 sin 2x))
questions.solution: √(2 sin 2x) = 2√(sin x cos x) = 2cos x √(tan x). So the integrand is sec⁴x/(2√tan x) = (1 + tan²x)sec²x/(2√tan x). Put t = tan x: ∫₀¹ (1 + t²)/(2√t) dt = ½[2√t + (2/5)t^(5/2)]₀¹ = ½(2 + 2/5) = 6/5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Verify that the lines given by r = (1 − λ)i + (λ − 2)j + (3 − 2λ)k and r = (μ + 1)i + (2μ − 1)j − (2μ + 1)k are skew lines. Hence, find the shortest distance between the lines.
questions.solution: Line 1: a₁ = i − 2j + 3k, b₁ = −i + j − 2k. Line 2: a₂ = i − j − k, b₂ = i + 2j − 2k. b₁ × b₂ = 2i − 4j − 3k (|b₁ × b₂| = √29), so the lines are not parallel. a₂ − a₁ = j − 4k, and (a₂ − a₁)·(b₁ × b₂) = −4 + 12 = 8 ≠ 0, so they do not meet: they are skew. Shortest distance = 8/√29 units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: During a cricket match, the positions of the bowler, the wicket keeper and the leg slip fielder are in a line given by B = 2i + 8j, W = 6i + 12j and F = 12i + 18j respectively. Calculate the ratio in which the wicket keeper divides the line segment joining the bowler and the leg slip fielder.
questions.solution: Let W divide BF in the ratio k : 1. Then (12k + 2)/(k + 1) = 6, so 6k = 4 and k = 2/3. Check: (18k + 8)/(k + 1) = 20/(5/3) = 12. The ratio is 2 : 3 (internally).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If √(1 − x²) + √(1 − y²) = a(x − y), then prove that dy/dx = √((1 − y²)/(1 − x²)).
questions.solution: Put x = sin A, y = sin B. Then cos A + cos B = a(sin A − sin B), i.e. 2cos((A+B)/2)cos((A−B)/2) = 2a cos((A+B)/2)sin((A−B)/2). So cot((A − B)/2) = a and A − B = 2cot⁻¹ a, i.e. sin⁻¹x − sin⁻¹y = constant. Differentiating, 1/√(1 − x²) − (1/√(1 − y²)) dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = √(1 − y²)/√(1 − x²).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If x = a(cos θ + log tan(θ/2)) and y = sin θ, then find d²y/dx² at θ = π/4.
questions.solution: dx/dθ = a(−sin θ + 1/sin θ) = a cos²θ/sin θ and dy/dθ = cos θ, so dy/dx = tan θ / a. Then d²y/dx² = (sec²θ / a) · dθ/dx = (sec²θ/a)(sin θ/(a cos²θ)) = sin θ/(a² cos⁴θ). At θ = π/4: (1/√2)/(a² · 1/4) = 2√2/a².

questions.text: Find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum of the function f(x) = 2x³ − 15x² + 36x + 1 on [1, 5].
questions.solution: f′(x) = 6x² − 30x + 36 = 6(x − 2)(x − 3), critical points 2 and 3. f(1) = 24, f(2) = 29, f(3) = 28, f(5) = 56. Absolute maximum 56 at x = 5; absolute minimum 24 at x = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the image A′ of the point A(1, 6, 3) in the line x/1 = (y − 1)/2 = (z − 2)/3. Also, find the equation of the line joining A and A′.
questions.solution: A general point of the line is P(λ, 1 + 2λ, 2 + 3λ). AP = (λ − 1, 2λ − 5, 3λ − 1) is perpendicular to (1, 2, 3): 14λ − 14 = 0, so λ = 1 and the foot is (1, 3, 5). A′ = 2(1, 3, 5) − (1, 6, 3) = (1, 0, 7). Line AA′: direction (0, −6, 4) ∝ (0, −3, 2), so x = 1, (y − 6)/(−3) = (z − 3)/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A school wants to allocate students into three clubs : Sports, Music and Drama, under the following conditions :
• The number of students in the Sports club should be equal to the sum of the number of students in the Music and Drama clubs.
• The number of students in the Music club should be 20 more than half the number of students in the Sports club.
• The total number of students to be allocated in all three clubs is 180.
Find the number of students allocated to the different clubs, using the matrix method.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A technical company is designing a rectangular solar panel installation on a roof using 300 metres of boundary material. The design includes a partition running parallel to one of the sides dividing the area (roof) into two sections. Let the length of the side perpendicular to the partition be x metres and the side parallel to the partition be y metres.

Write the equation for the total boundary material used in the boundary and parallel to the partition in terms of x and y.
questions.solution: Two sides of length x, two of length y and the partition of length y: 2x + 3y = 300.

questions.text:
A technical company is designing a rectangular solar panel installation on a roof using 300 metres of boundary material. The design includes a partition running parallel to one of the sides dividing the area (roof) into two sections. Let the length of the side perpendicular to the partition be x metres and the side parallel to the partition be y metres.

Find the critical points of the area function. Use the second derivative test to determine the critical points at the maximum area. Also, find the maximum area.
questions.solution: A′(x) = 100 − (4/3)x = 0 gives x = 75. A″(x) = −4/3 < 0, so the area is maximum at x = 75 (then y = 50). Maximum area = 75 × 50 = 3750 m².

Using the first derivative test, calculate the maximum area the company can enclose with the 300 metres of boundary material, considering the parallel partition.
questions.solution: A′(x) = 100 − (4/3)x is positive for x < 75 and negative for x > 75, so A is maximum at x = 75, y = 50. Maximum area = 3750 m².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A bank offers loans to its customers on different types of interest namely, fixed rate, floating rate and variable rate. From past data it is known that a customer avails a loan on fixed rate, floating rate or variable rate with probabilities 10%, 20% and 70% respectively. A customer after availing a loan can pay the loan or default on loan repayment. The bank data suggests that the probability that a person defaults after availing the loan at fixed rate, floating rate and variable rate is 5%, 3% and 1% respectively.

What is the probability that a customer after availing the loan will default on the loan repayment?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A bank offers loans to its customers on different types of interest namely, fixed rate, floating rate and variable rate. From past data it is known that a customer avails a loan on fixed rate, floating rate or variable rate with probabilities 10%, 20% and 70% respectively. A customer after availing a loan can pay the loan or default on loan repayment. The bank data suggests that the probability that a person defaults after availing the loan at fixed rate, floating rate and variable rate is 5%, 3% and 1% respectively.

A customer after availing the loan defaults on loan repayment. What is the probability that he availed the loan at a variable rate of interest?
questions.solution: By Bayes' theorem: P(variable | D) = 0.007/0.018 = 7/18.
